text: Salmon distinguishes a genuine causal process, which transmits a conserved quantity, from a mere ___, such as a shadow moving across a wall or a spot of light sweeping a screen, which transmits nothing and can even move faster than light.
explanation: A pseudo-process merely moves without transmitting energy, momentum, or any conserved quantity, so it can exceed light speed and carries no causal influence, unlike a genuine causal process. Dowe later refined this into the conserved quantity theory, on which causal processes are world-lines possessing conserved quantities and causal interactions are exchanges of them.
